problem.summary: 图像恢复是一个长期存在的低层视觉问题，旨在从低质量图像（如降采样、噪声和压缩图像）中恢复高质量图像。

motivation.summary: 当前最先进的图像恢复方法基于卷积神经网络（CNN），但CNN存在两个基本问题：1）图像与卷积核的交互是内容无关的，使用相同的卷积核恢复不同图像区域可能不是最佳选择；2）在局部处理原则下，卷积对长距离依赖建模效果不佳。Transformer在高层视觉任务中表现出色，但在图像恢复领域尝试较少。

core_idea.summary: 提出基于Swin Transformer的强基线模型SwinIR用于图像恢复。SwinIR由三部分组成：浅层特征提取、深层特征提取和高质量图像重建。深层特征提取模块由多个残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）组成，每个RSTB包含多个Swin Transformer层和一个残差连接。

method.summary: SwinIR网络架构包含三个模块：浅层特征提取（使用卷积层提取浅层特征）、深层特征提取（由K个残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）和一个3×3卷积层组成）、高质量图像重建（聚合浅层和深层特征）。RSTB由多个Swin Transformer层（STL）和卷积层组成，STL基于局部注意力和移位窗口机制。损失函数根据任务不同使用L1像素损失或Charbonnier损失。

experiments.summary: 在三个代表性任务上进行实验：图像超分辨率（包括经典、轻量级和真实世界图像超分辨率）、图像去噪（包括灰度和彩色图像去噪）和JPEG压缩伪影减少。实验结果表明SwinIR在不同任务上优于最先进方法，PSNR提升高达0.14-0.45dB，同时参数总数可减少高达67%。

claims.claim: SwinIR在图像超分辨率、图像去噪和JPEG压缩伪影减少任务上达到最先进性能。
SwinIR比基于CNN的方法更高效，参数更少但性能更好。
SwinIR能够有效建模长距离依赖，同时保持局部注意力的优势。
SwinIR在训练数据较少时也能取得良好性能，不像IPT那样严重依赖大规模数据集。
SwinIR的残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）设计有效，其中的卷积层增强了平移等变性。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论SwinIR的局限性，但根据内容可推断：1）对于真实世界图像超分辨率，由于缺乏真实高质量图像，仅提供视觉比较；2）模型在处理非常大的图像时可能面临计算效率问题；3）论文主要关注特定任务，未探讨更广泛的图像恢复应用。

nodes.title: 浅层特征提取模块
nodes.label: Shallow Feature Extraction
nodes.summary: 使用卷积层从低质量输入图像中提取浅层特征，这些特征直接传递到重建模块以保留低频信息。
nodes.description: 浅层特征提取模块使用一个卷积层将输入图像空间映射到更高维的特征空间，提取浅层特征F0。卷积层擅长早期视觉处理，能带来更稳定的优化和更好的结果，并提供一种简单的方式将输入图像空间映射到更高维特征空间。

nodes.title: 深层特征提取模块
nodes.label: Deep Feature Extraction
nodes.summary: 由多个残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）和一个3×3卷积层组成，用于从浅层特征中提取深层特征。
nodes.description: 深层特征提取模块包含K个残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）和一个3×3卷积层。中间特征F1, F2, ..., FK和输出深层特征FDF逐块提取。使用卷积层在特征提取末端可以将卷积操作的归纳偏置引入基于Transformer的网络，并为后续浅层和深层特征的聚合奠定更好的基础。

nodes.title: 残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）
nodes.label: Residual Swin Transformer Block (RSTB)
nodes.summary: RSTB由多个Swin Transformer层（STL）和一个卷积层组成，通过残差连接聚合特征。
nodes.description: RSTB包含L个Swin Transformer层（STL）和一个卷积层。STL用于局部注意力和跨窗口交互。RSTB的输出通过卷积层和残差连接计算：Fi,out = HCONVi(Fi,L) + Fi,0。这种设计有两个好处：1）卷积层增强了SwinIR的平移等变性；2）残差连接提供了从不同块到重建模块的恒等连接，允许聚合不同级别的特征。

nodes.title: Swin Transformer层（STL）
nodes.label: Swin Transformer Layer (STL)
nodes.summary: 基于标准多头自注意力，但采用局部注意力和移位窗口机制来建模长距离依赖。
nodes.description: STL基于标准多头自注意力，主要区别在于局部注意力和移位窗口机制。给定输入H×W×C，Swin Transformer首先将输入重塑为非重叠M×M局部窗口，然后为每个窗口单独计算标准自注意力（即局部注意力）。通过交替使用常规和移位窗口分区来实现跨窗口连接。

nodes.title: 高质量图像重建模块
nodes.label: HQ Image Reconstruction
nodes.summary: 聚合浅层和深层特征以重建高质量图像，使用子像素卷积层进行上采样（对于超分辨率任务）。
nodes.description: 重建模块通过聚合浅层特征F0和深层特征FDF来重建高质量图像IRHQ：IRHQ = HREC(F0 + FDF)。浅层特征主要包含低频信息，深层特征专注于恢复丢失的高频信息。通过长跳跃连接，SwinIR可以直接将低频信息传递到重建模块，帮助深层特征提取模块专注于高频信息并稳定训练。对于图像超分辨率，使用子像素卷积层进行上采样；对于不需要上采样的任务（如去噪和JPEG伪影减少），使用单个卷积层。

nodes.title: 损失函数
nodes.label: Loss Function
nodes.summary: 根据任务不同使用L1像素损失或Charbonnier损失进行优化。
nodes.description: 对于图像超分辨率，使用L1像素损失：L = ||IRHQ - IHQ||1。对于真实世界图像超分辨率，使用像素损失、GAN损失和感知损失的组合。对于图像去噪和JPEG压缩伪影减少，使用Charbonnier损失：L = sqrt(||IRHQ - IHQ||^2 + ε^2)，其中ε经验设置为10^-3。

edges.label: 浅层特征输入到深层特征提取

浅层特征直接传递到重建模块

deltas.before: CNN方法使用卷积核进行特征提取，交互内容无关，长距离依赖建模能力有限。
deltas.after: SwinIR使用Swin Transformer层（STL）进行局部注意力和跨窗口交互，能有效建模长距离依赖。
deltas.why_it_matters: 解决了CNN的两个基本问题：内容无关交互和长距离依赖建模不足，提升了图像恢复性能。

deltas.before: IPT方法依赖大规模数据集（超过1.1M图像）和多任务学习，参数量巨大（115.5M）。
deltas.after: SwinIR参数量小（11.8M），在较小数据集（如DIV2K）上也能取得良好性能，甚至优于IPT。
deltas.why_it_matters: SwinIR更高效，不严重依赖大规模数据集，更适合实际应用。

deltas.before: 传统Transformer使用全局自注意力，计算复杂度高，不适合处理大尺寸图像。
deltas.after: SwinIR采用局部注意力和移位窗口机制，降低了计算复杂度，同时保持了建模长距离依赖的能力。
deltas.why_it_matters: 使Transformer能够高效处理图像恢复任务，平衡了性能和计算效率。

deltas.before: CNN方法中的注意力机制（如通道注意力、非局部注意力）性能有限。
deltas.after: SwinIR基于Transformer的注意力机制（局部注意力）在图像恢复任务上表现更优。
deltas.why_it_matters: 证明了Transformer注意力机制在低层视觉任务中的有效性。

deltas.before: RSTB设计：无残差连接或仅使用卷积层。
deltas.after: RSTB包含卷积层和残差连接，增强了平移等变性并允许特征聚合。
deltas.why_it_matters: 提升了模型性能和训练稳定性。

formulas.intuition: 从浅层特征中提取深层特征，用于恢复高频信息。
逐块提取深层特征，每个RSTB包含多个Swin Transformer层。

聚合浅层和深层特征以重建高质量图像，浅层特征保留低频信息，深层特征恢复高频信息。
SwinIR的最终输出是通过残差学习得到的，即网络学习残差然后加到输入上。
用于图像超分辨率的L1像素损失，优化重建图像与真实图像之间的差异。
用于图像去噪和JPEG压缩伪影减少的Charbonnier损失，比L1损失更平滑。

glossary.Swin Transformer: 一种基于移位窗口的Transformer架构，通过局部注意力和跨窗口连接高效建模长距离依赖。
glossary.残差Swin Transformer块（RSTB）: SwinIR的核心构建块，包含多个Swin Transformer层和一个卷积层，通过残差连接聚合特征。
glossary.Swin Transformer层（STL）: 基于标准多头自注意力，但采用局部注意力和移位窗口机制的Transformer层。
glossary.局部注意力: 在非重叠的局部窗口内计算自注意力，降低计算复杂度。
glossary.移位窗口机制: 通过交替使用常规和移位窗口分区来实现跨窗口连接，增强模型建模长距离依赖的能力。
glossary.浅层特征提取: 使用卷积层从输入图像中提取低频信息，直接传递到重建模块。
glossary.深层特征提取: 由多个RSTB组成，从浅层特征中提取高频信息用于恢复。
glossary.高质量图像重建: 聚合浅层和深层特征以重建高质量图像，使用子像素卷积层进行上采样（对于超分辨率任务）。
glossary.L1像素损失: 重建图像与真实图像之间的绝对误差损失，用于图像超分辨率。
glossary.Charbonnier损失: 一种平滑的L1损失变体，用于图像去噪和JPEG压缩伪影减少。
glossary.子像素卷积层: 一种上采样方法，通过卷积和像素重排增加特征图分辨率。
glossary.平移等变性: 模型对输入图像平移的响应具有等变性，卷积层天然具有此性质。

steps.description: 1. 准备数据集：下载DIV2K、Flickr2K等训练数据集和相应测试数据集。
2. 实现SwinIR网络架构：包括浅层特征提取、深层特征提取（RSTB）和高质量图像重建模块。
3. 实现损失函数：根据任务选择L1像素损失或Charbonnier损失。
4. 训练模型：使用训练数据集训练SwinIR，调整超参数（如通道数、RSTB数量、STL数量等）。
5. 评估模型：在测试数据集上评估SwinIR的性能，计算PSNR/SSIM等指标。
6. 进行消融实验：验证RSTB设计、通道数、训练数据量等因素的影响。

metadata.title: SwinIR: Image Restoration Using Swin Transformer
metadata.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Computer Vision / Transformer / Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Image restoration is a long-standing low-level vision problem that aims to restore high-quality images from low-quality images (e.g., downscaled, noisy and compressed images). While state-of-the-art image restoration methods are based on convolutional neural networks, few attempts have been made with Transformers which show impressive performance on high-level vision tasks. In this paper, we propose a strong baseline model SwinIR for image restoration based on the Swin Transformer. SwinIR consists of three parts: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and high-quality image reconstruction. In particular, the deep feature extraction module is composed of several residual Swin Transformer blocks (RSTB), each of which has several Swin Transformer layers together with a residual connection. We conduct experiments on three representative tasks: image super-resolution (including classical, lightweight and real-world image super-resolution), image denoising (including grayscale and color image denoising) and JPEG compression artifact reduction. Experimental results demonstrate that SwinIR outperforms state-of-the-art methods on different tasks by up to 0.14鈭?.45dB, while the total number of parameters can be reduced by up to 67%.

Abstract

Image restoration is a long-standing low-level vision problem that aims to restore high-quality images from low- quality images (e.g., downscaled, noisy and compressed im- ages). While state-of-the-art image restoration methods are based on convolutional neural networks, few attempts have been made with Transformers which show impressive per- formance on high-level vision tasks. In this paper , we pro- pose a strong baseline model SwinIR for image restora- tion based on the Swin Transformer . SwinIR consists of three parts: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extrac- tion and high-quality image reconstruction. In particular , the deep feature extraction module is composed of several residual Swin Transformer blocks (RSTB), each of which has several Swin Transformer layers together with a resid- ual connection. We conduct experiments on three represen- tative tasks: image super-resolution (including classical, lightweight and real-world image super-resolution), image denoising (in...

First, the interactions between images and convolution kernels are content-independent. Using the same convolution kernel to restore different image regions may not be the best choice. Second, under the principle of local processing, convolution is not effective for long-range dependency modelling. As an alternative to CNN, Transformer [76] designs a self-attention mechanism to capture global interactions be- tween contexts and has shown promising performance in several vision problems [6, 74, 19, 56]. However, vision Transformers for image restoration [9, 5] usually divide the input image into patches with ﬁxed size ( e.g., 48×48) and process each patch independently. Such a strategy in- evitably gives rise to two drawbacks. First, border pixels cannot utilize neighbouring pixels that are out of the patch for image restoration....

In this paper, we propose an image restoration model, namely SwinIR, based on Swin Transformer. More specif- ically, SwinIR consists of three modules: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and high-quality image reconstruction modules. Shallow feature extraction module uses a convolution layer to extract shallow feature, which is directly transmitted to the reconstruction module so as to preserve low-frequency information. Deep feature extrac- tion module is mainly composed of residual Swin Trans- former blocks (RSTB), each of which utilizes several Swin Transformer layers for local attention and cross-window in- teraction. In addition, we add a convolution layer at the end of the block for feature enhancement and use a resid- ual connection to provide a shortcut for feature aggregation. Finally, both shallow and deep features are fused in the re- construction module for high-quality image reconstruction. Compared with prevalent CNN-based image restoration models, Transf...

Some of them have exploited the attention mechanism inside the CNN framework, such as channel attention [95, 15, 63], non-local attention [52, 61] and adaptive patch aggrega- tion [100]. 2.2. Vision Transformer Recently, natural language processing model Trans- former [76] has gained much popularity in the computer vision community. When used in vision problems such as image classiﬁcation [66, 19, 84, 56, 45, 55, 75], ob- ject detection [6, 53, 74, 56], segmentation [84, 99, 56, 4] and crowd counting [47, 69], it learns to attend to impor- tant...

Besides, both IPT and VSR-Transformer are patch-wise at- tention, which may be improper for image restoration. In addition, a concurrent work [82] proposed a U-shaped ar- chitecture based on the Swin Transformer [56]. 3. Method 3.1. Network Architecture As shown in Fig. 2, SwinIR consists of three modules: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and high- quality (HQ) image reconstruction modules. We employ the same feature extraction modules for all restoration tasks, but use different reconstruction modules for different tasks. Shallow and deep feature extraction. Image reconstruction. Taking image SR as an example, we reconstruct the high-quality image IRHQ by aggregating shallow and deep features as
IRHQ =HREC(F0 +FDF), (4)

where HREC(·) is the function of the reconstruction mod- ule. Shallow feature mainly contain low-frequencies, while deep feature focus on recovering lost high-frequencies. With a long skip connection, SwinIR can transmit the low- frequency information directly to the reconstruction mod- ule, which can help deep feature extraction module focus on high-frequency information and stabilize training. For the implementation of reconstruction module, we use the sub-pixel convolution layer [68] to upsample the feature. For tasks that do not need upsampling, such as image denoising and JPEG compression artifact reduction, a single convolution layer is used for reconstruction. Besides, we use residual learning to reconstruct the residual between the LQ and the HQ image instead of the HQ image. This is formulated as
IRHQ =HSwinIR(ILQ) +ILQ, (5)
whereHSwinIR(·) denotes the function of SwinIR. Loss function. For image SR, we optimize the parameters

whereIRHQ is obtained by takingILQ as the input of SwinIR, andIHQ is the corresponding ground-truth HQ image. For classical and lightweight image SR, we only use the naive L1 pixel loss as same as previous work to show the effec- tiveness of the proposed network. For real-world image SR, we use a combination of pixel loss, GAN loss and percep- tual loss [81, 89, 80, 27, 39, 81] to improve visual quality. For image denoising and JPEG compression artifact re- duction, we use the Charbonnier loss [8] L = √ ∥IRHQ−IHQ∥2 +ϵ2, (7) whereϵ is a constant that is empirically set to 10−3. 3.2. Given the input fea- tureFi,0 of thei-th RSTB, we ﬁrst extract intermediate fea- turesFi,1,Fi,2,...,F i,L byL Swin Transformer layers as
whereHSTLi,j (·) is the j-th Swin Transformer layer in the i-th RSTB. Then, we add a convolutional layer before the residual connection. The output of RSTB is formulated as
Fi,out =HCONVi (Fi,L) +Fi,0, (9)

where HCONVi (·) is the convolutional layer in the i-th RSTB. This design has two beneﬁts. First, although Trans- former can be viewed as a speciﬁc instantiation of spatially varying convolution [21, 75], covolutional layers with spa- tially invariant ﬁlters can enhance the translational equivari- ance of SwinIR. Second, the residual connection provides a identity-based connection from different blocks to the re- construction module, allowing the aggregation of different levels of features. 3

Swin Transformer layer . Swin Transformer layer (STL) [56] is based on the standard multi-head self- attention of the original Transformer layer [76]. The main differences lie in local attention and the shifted window mechanism. As shown in Fig. 2(b), given an input of size H×W×C, Swin Transformer ﬁrst reshapes the input to a HW M 2 × M 2× C feature by partitioning the input into non-overlappingM×M local windows, where HW M 2 is the total number of windows. Then, it computes the standard self-attention separately for each window ( i.e., local atten- tion). For a local window feature X∈ RM 2×C, the query, key and value matricesQ,K andV are computed as
Q =XPQ, K =XPK, V =XPV, (10)

where PQ, PK and PV are projection matrices that are shared across different windows. Generally, we have Q,K,V ∈ RM 2×d. The attention matrix is thus computed by the self-attention mechanism in a local window as
Attention(Q,K,V ) = SoftMax(QKT/

√ d +B)V, (11) where B is the learnable relative positional encoding. In practice, following [76], we perform the attention function forh times in parallel and concatenate the results for multi- head self-attention (MSA). Next, a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) that has two fully- connected layers with GELU non-linearity between them is used for further feature transformations. The LayerNorm (LN) layer is added before both MSA and MLP, and the residual connection is employed for both modules. The whole process is formulated as
X = MSA(LN(X)) +X,
X = MLP(LN(X)) +X. (12)

However, when the partition is ﬁxed for different lay- ers, there is no connection across local windows. There- fore, regular and shifted window partitioning are used al- ternately to enable cross-window connections [56], where shifted window partitioning means shifting the feature by (⌊M 2⌋,⌊M 2⌋) pixels before partitioning. 4. As we can see, our method can remove heavy noise cor- ruption and preserve high-frequency image details, result- ing in sharper edges and more natural textures. By contrast, other methods suffer from either over-smoothness or over- sharpness, and cannot recover rich textures. 5. Conclusion In this paper, we propose a Swin Transformer-based im- age restoration model SwinIR. The model is composed of three parts: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extrac- 7

In particular, we use a stack of residual Swin Transformer blocks (RSTB) for deep feature extraction, and each RSTB is composed of Swin Transformer layers, convolution layer and a residual con- nection. Extensive experiments show that SwinIR achieves state-of-the-art performance on three representative image restoration tasks and six different settings: classic image SR, lightweight image SR, real-world image SR, grayscale image denoising, color image denoising and JPEG com- pression artifact reduction, which demonstrates the effec- tiveness and generalizability of the proposed SwinIR.
